title: Health-weighted cohort orchestration for progressive upgrades and auto-rollback
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Introduce a health-weighted cohort orchestration subsystem for progressive upgrades. Instead of purely time- or percentage-based ramps, routing weight will be adjusted in near-real-time according to an aggregated health score for each cohort (region, customer tier, runtime pool). The goal is to make canaries and percent ramps materially more responsive to observed regressions while preserving predictable ramp behavior for healthy cohorts.

This ticket covers design and implementation of the core control loop, operator controls (console + API), and automated rollback triggers. The system will: compute per-cohort health scores from latency/error/accuracy indicators, use a configurable weighting function to convert health into allowed ramp velocity, and drive traffic routing through the existing routing plane with minimal latency. Auto-rollback will be driven by sequential hypothesis tests (SPRT) on primary health metrics plus hard-threshold safety nets.

We need tight integration with the Console (rollout UI) so SREs and PMs can visualize the cohort health curves, change policies, and apply temporary hold/force-rollbacks. We'll also add a TTL-based operator override mechanism to allow short-term manual interventions that auto-expire. The feature must be compatible with LTS/patch channels (ability to pin cohorts to LTS channel versions and exclude them from automated ramps), and should produce clear audit entries for every automated decision (ramp up/down/rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Health-weighted orchestration control loop implemented and running in staging; cohorts defined by region/customer-tier/pool
Routing plane accepts dynamic weight updates and applies changes within 1s of decision
Configurable weighting functions available (linear, sigmoid, capped velocity) and selectable per project
SPRT-based auto-rollback correctly triggers on synthetic and real-failure signals in canary tests
Console UI shows cohort health time-series, current weight, and last automated action; operator can apply TTL overrides
All automated decisions are logged to the audit store with operator-visible reasoning and links to diagnostics
Unit/integration tests for control loop, metric ingestion, and rollback logic; load test showing no >1% added p99 latency on path
Compatibility with LTS channels: cohorts pinned to LTS must be excluded from auto-ramp and must surface a clear warning in Console
implementation_plan: Design doc: health score composition and weighting function (owner: Maya) — link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RP/Health-Weighted-Orchestration
Schema: define cohort metadata and policy CRD for control plane (owner: Liam)
Metrics: extend runtime to emit per-cohort latency/error/accuracy metrics and signal sinks (owner: infra)
Control loop: implement decision engine with configurable policy, SPRT tests, and TTL override support (owner: runtime-team)
Routing: small API to accept incremental weight diffs; integrate with existing smart routing and fallback policies
Console: rollout UI changes (health chart, policy editor, overrides), plus audit viewer (owner: dx)
E2E: synthetic canary scenarios + chaos experiments to validate rollback and hold behavior
Docs: runbook for operators, migration guide for customers wanting cohort tags and LTS exclusions
Security: review audit trails and access controls (SOC review if needed)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics can cause oscillations. Mitigation: smoothing window + hysteresis + capped velocity for weight adjustments.

Risk: control loop bugs could mis-route large traffic. Mitigation: start with staging-only, then small percentage pilot, and a safety circuit-breaker that immediately freezes ramps on rule violations.
Risk: operator confusion with automated overrides. Mitigation: TTL-based overrides that auto-expire and clear UI affordances + audit entries.
Risk: interaction with LTS pinning causing unexpected behavior. Mitigation: explicit exclusion rules and preflight checks in Console when enabling health-weighted policy.
testing_plan: Unit tests for weighting functions and SPRT implementation
Integration tests: metric ingestion -> decision -> routing weight update path
Staging canary: run two revisions across cohorts with injected latencies/errors to validate ramp slowdown and rollback
Load tests: verify decision loop and routing API under production-like QPS
Chaos tests: randomized transient failures and coordinated region outages to validate safety circuit-breaker
